classification_rules: COST_ROBUST: edge at gross & realistic_1x & stress_2x for some lookback; COST_FRAGILE: edge at gross & realistic_1x but not stress_2x; COST_ELIMINATED: gross edge not an edge at realistic_1x; NO_EDGE: no gross edge; ANOMALOUS: edge only under costs.
signal_characterization_note: momentum_signals uses np.mean(np.log(closes[i-lookback+1:i+1])) -- the mean log PRICE over the window, not the mean log return. For all collected large-cap prices (> $1) this mean is positive, so the realized weight is +1 on every non-neutral bar (turnover_diagnostic shows n_short=0 and <=1 sign flip per asset). The 'momentum' signal is therefore effectively constant-long, and the cost grid reflects only constant-dollar rebalancing cost, not directional turnover. The cost-robustness classification is valid for the signal as implemented; it must NOT be read as evidence that a direction-dependent short-horizon momentum strategy survives costs.
